title: Page induction
statement:
Let $\varphi:E\to E'$ be a morphism of spectral sequences
[def-sp-spectral-sequence] with pages $E_r$, $E'_r$ for $r\geq2$. If $\varphi$ is an
isomorphism on the $E_2$-page in every bidegree, then it is an isomorphism on
every page $E_r$, $2\leq r<\infty$. If moreover $E_\infty$ and $E'_\infty$ exist, formed
as $Z_\infty/B_\infty$ by the recursive cycle and boundary subobjects of
[def-sp-convergence] (that construction uses only the pages $E_r=Z_r/B_r$ and the
differentials $d_r$, and is applied here to $E$ and $E'$ component by component), then
$\varphi$ also induces an isomorphism $E_\infty\cong E'_\infty$.

proof.text: By [def-sp-spectral-sequence], every page $E_r$ is a complex with differential $d_r$, and the specified identification of its homology with $E_{r+1}$ is compatible with morphisms of spectral sequences. Thus the page map $\varphi_r$ is a chain map and the next page map is the map induced on homology under these identifications.

The map on page $2$ is an isomorphism by hypothesis. If $\varphi_r$ is an isomorphism, its commutation with $d_r$ identifies the kernels of the differentials and the images of the differentials on the two complexes; therefore it induces an isomorphism on the quotient $\ker(d_r)/\operatorname{im}(d_r)$, i.e. on homology. The compatible page identifications from Step 1 then make $\varphi_{r+1}$ an isomorphism. Induction on $r$ proves that $\varphi_r$ is an isomorphism for every finite $r\ge2$.

By [def-sp-convergence], the cycle and boundary subobjects $B_r\subseteq Z_r\subseteq E_2$ are defined recursively by $Z_2=E_2$, $B_2=0$, and $Z_{r+1}$, $B_{r+1}$ the inverse images of $\ker d_r$ and $\operatorname{im}d_r$ under $Z_r\twoheadrightarrow E_r=Z_r/B_r$; the limiting page is $E_\infty=Z_\infty/B_\infty$ with $Z_\infty=\bigcap_r Z_r$ and $B_\infty=\bigcup_r B_r$ when these limits exist. By induction on $r$, the isomorphism $\varphi_2$ maps $Z_r$ onto $Z'_r$ and $B_r$ onto $B'_r$, and the map it induces on $Z_r/B_r$ is $\varphi_r$: this holds for $r=2$, and if it holds for $r$, then since $\varphi_r$ commutes with $d_r$ and is an isomorphism (Step 2) it maps $\ker d_r$ onto $\ker d'_r$ and $\operatorname{im}d_r$ onto $\operatorname{im}d'_r$, so $\varphi_2$ maps their inverse images $Z_{r+1}$, $B_{r+1}$ onto $Z'_{r+1}$, $B'_{r+1}$, and the induced map on the quotient is $\varphi_{r+1}$ by Step 1. An isomorphism $E_2\cong E'_2$ carries intersections and unions of subobjects to intersections and unions, so $\varphi_2(Z_\infty)=Z'_\infty$ and $\varphi_2(B_\infty)=B'_\infty$, and $\varphi_2$ induces an isomorphism $E_\infty=Z_\infty/B_\infty\cong Z'_\infty/B'_\infty=E'_\infty$.
